{"id":"486ed53d-4f3e-47db-8050-c1a63e71797f","object":"chat.completion","created":1790510270,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"parent_requirement_id": "R3", "mode": "residual", "used_claims": ["C2", "C3"], "local_residual": "Establish whether Evita Manji, as Sophie's partner at the time of Sophie's death, gave an interview in which she said that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs, rather than only making the posthumous tribute statement reported in C3."}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need identify one coherent evidence objective inside Parent Requirement R3. We have claims C2 partner Evita Manji, C3 tribute quote. Parent requirement: The partner of artist at time of death gave interview where they said that following their death, artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs. Need establish remaining part? Claim C2 establishes partner is Evita Manji (for Sophie presumably). Claim C3 establishes a later online tribute by partner, quote about immaterial girl, but not "interview", not "direct reference to one of their songs", not song title adjective. Need choose exactly one residual. We need not solve whole. We need local_residual.

Original question context: musical artist Sophie? Claims mention Sophie and partner Evita Manji. R3 says partner gave an interview where they said following death artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs. Need identify what still needs evidence. C3 provides a tribute? It says "In a later online tribute, Sophie's partner Evita Manji said..." That may partially support partner statement following death. But is it an interview? The parent says "gave an interview". C3 says online tribute, maybe not interview. Also "artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs" not supported; C3 quote "immaterial girl now; she can be anything..." Maybe direct reference to song "Immaterial"? Actually Sophie song "Immaterial" maybe. But cannot use outside. The quote contains "immaterial girl" but claim does not state direct reference to a song. We must not add outside. We need local residual: establish that Evita Manji gave an interview (not just online tribute) where she said Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs. Or maybe establish the direct reference to one of their songs. Which one coherent? The parent requirement has multiple semantic conditions: partner at time of death gave an interview; in it said following death artist became direct reference to one song. C2 establishes partner. C3 establishes partner said something in online tribute. Unresolved: whether it was an interview, and whether statement was direct reference to one of their songs. We should choose one coherent residual. Since claims already identify partner, maybe residual target: the interview statement that the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs. But that bundles interview and statement? "gave an interview where they said..." The key missing is the content: direct reference to one of their songs. We can phrase one objective: establish whether Evita Manji, in an interview following Sophie's death, said that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs. That is basically parent requirement, but maybe too broad? The instructions: choose exactly ONE coherent evidence objective inside Parent Requirement that still needs to be established. It may include relation. We can preserve participant roles. Used claims C2, C3? C3 partially supports quote but not direct reference. Used_claims should list claims used as established supporting for chosen residual? The output schema: used_claims. We can use C2 (partner identity) and maybe C3 (partner statement). But if C3 not fully supporting target, still context. The instruction says used_claims are "Verified Claims count as established evidence". If some part already established, don't ask again. C2 establishes partner. C3 establishes partner said tribute. So residual should avoid re-establishing partner identity and maybe avoid tribute? But maybe need establish that the statement was in an interview, not just online tribute, and specifically direct reference. If C3 says online tribute, not interview, then we cannot use C3 for interview. But C3 is a verified claim that partner made a statement after death. The parent says "gave an interview where they said..." C3 does not establish interview. So residual can be "that Evita Manji gave an interview (rather than only an online tribute) in which she said Sophie became a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." Is that one coherent objective? It includes both interview and content. Maybe split? The target is the quoted statement in an interview. Since no interview established, the content from interview is missing. We can ask: establish the content of Evita Manji's interview statement that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs. But to be faithful to parent, include partner role. Could mention "whether Evita Manji gave an interview where she said that, following Sophie's death, Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." That is the core residual. It doesn't re-ask partner identity. It uses C2, C3.

Need ensure not output search query, source, answer. JSON only.

Potential mode: residual, used_claims ["C2","C3"]? If C3 is not direct support, but used as context? The schema says used_claims list. In examples, if some part established, list claims. C3 establishes that partner made a later online tribute, but not interview. It may be used to mark part of parent (partner statement after death) partially supported. I'd include C2 and C3 because C2 establishes partner identity and C3 establishes a posthumous statement by partner, though not the interview/direct reference. The local_residual should say: "Establish whether Evita Manji, as Sophie's partner at the time of death, gave an interview in which she said that after Sophie's death Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs, specifically identifying the song relation." Hmm "specifically identifying the song relation" maybe not needed. The parent requirement doesn't require identifying title? It says direct reference to one of their songs. The original question ultimately asks title, but R3 only needs the statement that artist has become direct reference to one song. So residual: whether such an interview statement exists and says direct reference to one of the artist's songs. We can say "that the posthumous statement by Evita Manji was made in an interview and characterizes Sophie as a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." This is one objective. But it includes two attributes. Could be okay as single coherent evidence objective: the interview statement content.

Need maybe not mention "Sophie" if original question artist? Claims mention Sophie. Parent uses "the artist". We can use "Sophie" from claims. Fine.

Need return JSON only. Ensure valid JSON. 

Let's draft:

{
  "parent_requirement_id": "R3",
  "mode": "residual",
  "used_claims": ["C2", "C3"],
  "local_residual": "Establish whether Evita Manji, as Sophie's partner at the time of Sophie's death, gave an interview in which she said that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs."
}

Is that too broad? It includes interview and content. But parent requirement is exactly that. Since C3 says online tribute, not interview, so interview part unresolved. The "direct reference to one of their songs" unresolved. It's one coherent statement. Could be acceptable. But instruction: If several independent unresolved parts remain, choose exactly ONE coherent part. Do not bundle independent research objectives. Is "gave an interview" independent from "said direct reference"? Yes, but the parent requirement is a single relation: partner gave interview where said X. The residual is that exact relation. It might be considered bundling? Maybe choose one: "the content of the partner's statement: that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of her songs." But without interview, we might not know. The parent requirement's central missing evidence is the quoted statement. C3 already shows partner made a statement, but not direct reference. So maybe residual: "Establish that Evita Manji said (in an interview) that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." That still includes interview. If we omit interview, we may not satisfy parent. Hmm.

Maybe choose "whether the posthumous statement by Evita Manji referred to/characterized Sophie as a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." This is one coherent content objective. It preserves that it was said by partner following death. It doesn't require establishing interview format now. But parent says interview. However, if we ask content, the interview condition remains unresolved. The task says choose exactly one coherent evidence objective inside Parent Requirement that still needs to be established. So we can choose the content part. C3 says online tribute, which is a posthumous statement. So we can ask to establish whether that statement (or another interview) includes the direct-reference-to-song claim. That seems one objective. But the parent explicitly says "gave an interview where they said..." If we don't ask interview, we ignore one condition. That's okay, we're selecting one facet. The local residual should be low-commitment. Maybe:

"Establish whether Evita Manji's posthumous statement includes the claim that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs, as opposed to only the 'immaterial girl' wording reported in the tribute."

This uses C3 and targets the missing direct reference. It doesn't bundle interview. But parent says interview; we can mention "in an interview" maybe as context. Hmm.

The task: "identify exactly ONE coherent evidence objective inside the Parent Requirement that still needs to be established now." The Parent Requirement: "The partner ... gave an interview where they said that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." There are conditions:
1. partner at time of death (C2 established)
2. gave an interview
3. where they said following death artist has become direct reference to one song.

C3 establishes partner said something in online tribute, not necessarily interview, and not direct reference to song. So unresolved: 2 and 3. Which one is more central? The original question asks song title, but R3 is about interview quote. The direct reference to song is the key. The interview format might be needed to source the quote. But if C3 already has quote from online tribute, maybe the missing part is that in an interview she said the direct reference. Actually C3 quote doesn't mention song. So the missing evidence is the direct-reference-to-song statement. We can phrase local residual as: "Establish whether Evita Manji, in an interview after Sophie's death, said that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs (rather than only making the 'immaterial girl' tribute statement)." This is one objective. It includes interview and content but as a single quote. It's okay.

Need decide used_claims. If we mention "rather than only..." C3 used. C2 used. Good.

Maybe use mode residual. No need probe because substantive supporting claims exist (C2, C3). Yes.

Ensure no extra text. Final JSON.
